hypotheses.justification: Use an epsilon estimate instead of continuousAt_of_dominated. Each section is integrable on s: it is strongly measurable, bounded on the compact set s, and hs.measure_lt_top holds. IsCompact.mem_uniformity_of_prod gives, near any x₀, a uniform bound ‖f x y - f x₀ y‖ < δ for y ∈ s, without countability assumptions on X. Then integral_sub and norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const bound the integral difference by δ * μ.real s. Choose δ = ε / (μ.real s + 1). This also handles zero measure and empty s; empty X is vacuous. No completeness assumption is needed by these lemmas.

Compact neighborhoods in X can be avoided. IsCompact.mem_uniformity_of_prod, applied to hs and hf.continuousOn with parameter set univ, gives uniform closeness of f x and f x₀ on s near x₀ for arbitrary topological X. The sections are integrable by measurability, compact boundedness, and hs.measure_lt_top. Using integral_sub and norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const gives an integral difference bounded by δ * μ.real s, proving continuity. Choosing δ = ε / (μ.real s + 1) handles zero measure without division by zero; empty sets and empty X cause no problem. First countability and local compactness can both be deleted together.

Only the measurability step of the existing proof needs replacement. For each x, the continuous section g := f x is measurable after installing the Borel measurable structure on E, by Continuous.measurable. Its compact image K := g '' s is closed and separable. The measurable predicate g y ∈ K holds for every y ∈ s, so ae_restrict_iff shows it holds almost everywhere under μ.restrict s, even if s is not measurable. Thus aestronglyMeasurable_iff_aemeasurable_separable supplies the required AEStronglyMeasurable g (μ.restrict s), without second countability. The remaining proof is unchanged. For empty s the restricted measure is zero, also covered by this characterization.
